newsitem.title: USA: NCAA BASKETBALL-KENTUCKY TO FACE ARIZONA IN ALL-WILDCAT CHAMPIONSHIP GAME.
newsitem.headline: NCAA BASKETBALL-KENTUCKY TO FACE ARIZONA IN ALL-WILDCAT CHAMPIONSHIP GAME.

text.p: Defending champion Kentucky made it an all-Wildcat final by clawing out a 78-69 victory over the Minnesota Golden Gophers Saturday to earn a spot in Monday's title game against upstart Arizona.
"I have never coached a team with this much heart in my life," said Kentucky coach Rick Pitino.

Ron Mercer led the Kentucky Wildcats with 19 points on 7-for-21 shooting, but it was their snarling fullcourt defence that earned them the chance to defend their title against the surprising young Arizona Wildcats, 66-58 winners over the North Carolina Tar Heels in the night's first semifinal.
Kentucky had 14 steals to Minnesota's six and forced 26 turnovers while committing just 16 of their own.
Minnesota's brilliant guard Bobby Jackson led all scorers with 23 points on 8-for-18 shooting, 2-of-5 from three-point range.

Minnesota, which trailed by as many as 10 points in the first half, did not quit despite the unrelenting defensive pressure from Kentucky. The Gophers fought back to go ahead 52-51 with 10:45 left in the game.
But it was their only lead of the game.
Kentucky pulled away again to lead by as many as 12 points, then held on down the stretch.

"When they were pushed to the wall they came out and played aggressively," Pitino said of his team. "Without question this is the guttiest team I've ever coached. Remember there are three sophomores and a junior, really.
"We will have to play an unbelievable game Monday. Arizona has young players who play with no fear at all."
"We know right now we have our hands full, every player has their hands full because this is the quickest team I've seen in quite some time."

Arizona, seeded only fourth, became the surprise of the tournament when it knocked off mighty Kansas in the regional semifinals without a senior, but Pitino has been talking up what a surprise his team is, too.
The defending champions lost four players to the NBA and their leading scorer this season, Derek Anderson, to injury.

Pitino gave Anderson a cameo appearance, letting him shoot two technical free throws -- he made both -- in his first appearance since January 18 when he tore his anterior cruciate ligament against Auburn.

That technical foul, on Minnesota coach Clem Haskins after an offensive foul call on Courtney James, looked to be disastrous for the Gophers as their deficit went from four to eight on a Mercer side jumper following the free throws.
But Minnesota came alive, scoring nine straight points.
"Any time the coach gets a technical, I guess that kind of motivates us," said centre John Thomas.

Jackson hit a nifty reverse layup to cut the lead to 51-49, a Miles Tarver steal of a Kentucky inbound pass led to a Jackson three-pointer and the Gophers finally led, 52-51 with just inside 11 minutes to go.

But Mercer hit two free throws to put Kentucky back up at 53-52 and Wayne Turner made 1-of-2 foul shots to make it 54-52 before John Thomas converted an alley-oop from Jackson to tie it again at 54-54.

Kentucky then steadily pulled away, using a 6-0 run followed shortly by an 8-1 run to regain control. Three-pointers by Scott Padgett inside the six-minute mark and Cameron Mills with 4:19 to go were the key blows for the Wildcats.

Kentucky also won the free throw battle, making 23-of-34 foul shots (68 percent) to Minnesota's 12-of-19 (63 percent). The Wildcats calmly made 17-of-21 (81 percent) in the second half while Minnesota converted only 4-of-10 (40 percent).

"We beat a team that's as physically and mentally tough as any I've coached against since I've been at Kentucky," said Pitino. "They get up in your pants and they take you out of your offence. They're tough-minded."
He also gave credit to his guard Wayne Turner, who did a lot of the ball-handling and got five steals.
"I don't know how he did it, because he took on all that pressure and then then put pressure on them and played 39 minutes of great basketball with just one turnover.
Kentucky led 36-31 at the half. The Wildcats broke out 6-0, 14-5 and 27-17 but the Golden Gophers used a 6-1 run to close the half trailing 36-31.
"We came out and we were scared," said Jackson. "We had some careless turnovers, but we gave it all we could give. And that was the main point. We went out there and played our hearts out.
"And Coach was satisfied with the way we performed. And I was satisfied with the way we performed."
"I just want to give Kentucky the credit," said Haskins. "They did a super job of pressuring us, we didn't handle the pressure. you can't turn it over as many times as we turned it over."
